excerpt: Constant self-monitoring drains the energy that playfulness and flow need. Taking yourself less seriously turns out to be good for creativity and resilience.
summary: Francesca Tighinean argues that taking yourself too seriously carries a real psychological cost: constantly monitoring how others see you suppresses playful impulses and burns the mental energy that creative work and flow states depend on. Drawing on research linking playfulness to better cognition, resilience, and emotional regulation, she makes the case that adults who fold curiosity and play into ordinary activities, rather than saving it for scheduled leisure, think and feel better for it. A useful reminder for anyone whose work rewards intensity that the lighter touch is often the more effective one.
title: The Hidden Cost of Taking Yourself Too Seriously
